title: Clinical Trial Patient Intake & Consent Portal
idea: Build a clinical trial patient intake, multi-step eligibility screening, e-consent verification, and study coordinator review portal with protocol version tracking and an immutable audit trail.
problemStatement: Build a clinical trial patient intake, multi-step eligibility screening, e-consent verification, and study coordinator review portal with protocol version tracking and an immutable audit trail.

approaches.title: Approaches — Clinical Trial Patient Intake & Consent Portal

approaches.name: Rule-Checked Coordinator Workbench & Audit Ledger
approaches.summary: Structured screening checklist, IRB consent version tracker, PI review queue, and append-only audit log in one cohesive workbench.
approaches.bestFor: Multi-site clinical coordinators who need immediate eligibility feedback and regulatory auditability.
pros: Enforces inclusion, exclusion, and active IRB consent version rules before enrollment
Provides a dedicated PI sign-off queue for pending enrollments
Every state transition writes a queryable audit event automatically
cons: Requires relational schema across candidates, criteria responses, consents, and audit logs
risks: Must clearly explain why enrollment is blocked when any single criterion or consent version fails

approaches.name: Static Form Wizard with Manual Status
approaches.summary: Free-text intake notes and manual status dropdowns without criterion-level validation.
pros: Minimal schema and fast initial implementation
cons: Allows accidental enrollment of candidates with failed exclusion criteria
Cannot detect outdated IRB consent versions automatically
risks: High risk of protocol deviations during site audits

approaches.name: External BPMN State Engine
approaches.summary: Encode screening and consent workflows as external BPMN XML definitions.
approaches.bestFor: Enterprise CROs integrating dozens of legacy hospital systems.
cons: Heavy infrastructure overhead and poor UI responsiveness for coordinators
Splits validation logic away from the application database
risks: Schema drift between BPMN state variables and UI forms
